speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Minister for Health whether the Ministry will explore ways to upskill and enhance the capabilities of enrolled nurses and nursing aides, including those serving in nursing homes, through measures, such as training and certification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Enrolled Nurses (ENs) and support care staff, such as healthcare assistants and nursing aides, are important healthcare staff in the delivery of care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: They assist Registered Nurses (RNs) in the provision of nursing care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: ENs are able to carry out tasks, such as inserting stomach feeding tubes and blood glucose monitoring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: ENs and support care staff can undergo in-house training provided by our public healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: They can also attend courses offered by training providers, such as the SingHealth Alice Lee Institute of Advanced Nursing Studies and the Agency for Integrated Care's (AIC's) Learning Institute.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: ENs can also upskill to be RNs through the Diploma in Nursing course offered by Nanyang Polytechnic and Ngee Ann Polytechnic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to study ways to enhance the roles, professional growth and career pathways for our ENs and support care staff, so that we can continue to deliver good quality care for Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: At present, my residents tell me, and from my own experience in healthcare, a patient's caregiver can learn how to give an insulin injection under the skin.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: This may be a spouse or a loved one, but in essence, a layperson can be taught this skill through a short course.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, I was wondering whether MOH will consider making these courses available for nursing aides, especially at our nursing homes.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: This will help them upskill and also allow cross-training of staff and improve deployability.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Allow me to explain first, that while a diabetic patient is trained, he can be trained to give himself a specific type of insulin injection for self-care, or the caregiver could be trained to do so.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Healthcare staff, particularly those in healthcare institutions, are required to work with a broad range of different insulin on different patients, and this increases the need for safe care.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Although any medication used improperly can cause harm, high-alert medications cause harm more commonly, and the harm they produce is likely to be more serious and may lead to patients suffering and incurring additional costs associated with care of these patients.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, insulin injections, if wrongly administered, may cause the patient to go into a coma, and further complications can arise.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does MOH currently benchmark the level of professional training, specifically for nursing home staff, such as ENs and nursing aides, against other countries that may have a best practice in this area, like Japan, for example, which I think is known for high standards for eldercare and care in nursing homes, to see if there is scope to further improve the level of training and continuous training that nursing staff receive in Singapore nursing homes?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I suspect the level of training is rather uneven at the present moment when we look at the nursing home space.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, we do conduct study visits, as well as share information with healthcare institutions in different countries, including the Western developed countries, as well as Japan and Hong Kong.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It will also be looking at expanding the role and scope, and upskilling of healthcare support staff.
